title: Cleanup prioritization: signal dive (scratchpad)
content:
Context:
Quick personal scratch on how we should prioritize cleanup work for the next 3 sprints. Mostly thinking about the signals that indicate high-impact examples to fix vs low ROI noise. Use this to seed the triage rubric we discussed in triage sync.

Goal:
- Produce a small, actionable prioritization heuristic so labeling / micro-adjudication folks know what to surface to eng/product.
- Make sampling rules for weekly "clean pool" that QA team will run through (50-200 examples/week depending on capacity).

High-level principle:
Focus where model outputs (or downstream metrics) materially change product behavior or cost. Fixes that: reduce user-visible errors, reduce human-in-the-loop time, or cut token/retry costs.

Signals to bump priority (strong => urgent):
1) Regression on a tracked evaluation prompt set (we already have eval ids) - any drop >2% absolute on a metric tied to customer SLO.
2) Live customer escalation: documented examples from CS + reproduction in sandbox.
3) Examples that cause repeated model retries / hallucination loops (observed in logs; look for request ids with >1 generation).
4) High-frequency patterns in inference logs (same normalized canonical form occurs in top 1% of errors by count).
5) Cases that block automation (e.g., parsing invoice line items where downstream parser fails).

Signals to lower priority (deprioritize):
- Low-frequency one-off formatting oddities (unless they map to enterprise customer surface area).
- Cosmetic punctuation only (unless it impacts downstream ingestion).
- Language-style preferences isolated to a single locale we don't support yet.

Suggested prioritization score (simple, interpretable):
PriorityScore = freq_rank * customer_impact_weight * (1 + regen_penalty)
Where:
- freq_rank: 1 (rare) | 2 (occasional) | 3 (frequent) | 4 (very frequent)
- customer_impact_weight: 1 (none) | 2 (internal) | 3 (customer-facing) | 4 (blocker)
- regen_penalty: 0 if single-generation; 0.5 if observed retry loops; 1.0 if leads to >=2 retries
Notes: score range roughly 1-24. Anything >=12 => surface to product weekly. 6-12 => include in clean pool. <6 => backlog.

Examples and mini-decisions (actual examples anonymized):
- EX1: "Invoice: total = $1,234.00 
Items parsed: line1-> '1x blue-widget', line2-> 'discount: USD 50'" - Parser fails on 'discount' row because labeler heuristics treat 'discount' as item name.
  Decision: priority score = freq_rank 3 (we see 180 similar/month) * impact 4 (blocks accounting ingestion) * regen_penalty 0 => 12 => surface to product. Quick fix route: add explicit rule in parser and label guideline clarifying discount tokenization.

- EX2: Multi-sentence utterance where annotators disagree on whether to attach meta-tag 'intent: cancel' when user says 'maybe later' after initial cancel request.
  Decision: freq_rank 2 * impact 2 * regen_penalty 0 => 4 => backlog. Action: add ambiguous-intent adjudication examples to guideline, but not urgent.

Edgecases checklist (what to capture for each sample):
- Raw input snippet (truncate if PII)
- Model output that failed / why (parser error, hallucination, low confidence)
- Metric link if available (eval id / log id)
- Count of similar examples in last 30d (approx)
- Customer / product area impacted
- Proposed short mitigation (heuristic, annotation change, model prompt tweak, reroute)

Sampling rules for weekly clean pool (practical):
- 40%: high-ish freq, medium impact examples (freq_rank 2-3, impact 2-3)
- 30%: customer escalations / blockers (impact >=3)
- 20%: random stratified long-tail (to catch surprises)
- 10%: annotator-suspected ambiguous samples flagged during labeling UI

Quick heuristics for labelers to flag when triaging:
- "Parser mismatch": model claims structure but parser throws exception.
- "Stable hallucination": same incorrect fact across different prompts for same input.
- "Labeler confusion": >30% disagreement across 3 annotators for same sample.
- "Tokenization mismatch": entity boundary disagreements that shift downstream IDs.

Operational notes (to self):
- We need an RB to add fields in triage UI: 'freq_bucket', 'regen_seen', 'customer_scope'. Filing JIRA CURATE-742 (linked).
- For private deployment customers, mark examples with customer tag so we can prioritize enterprise SLAs (separate queue).
- Tagging conventions: use 'cleanup-urgent' for anything surfacing to product, 'cleanup-weekly' for pool.

Outstanding questions / TODOs:
- How to reliably compute freq_rank from logs without double-counting near-duplicates? (hashing canonicalized normalized form? need to prototype)
- Should we weigh cost savings (token reduction) directly into impact weight? Product asked for cost KPI but I think keep separate dimension for now.
- Confirm with SRE whether we can expose a small sample of generation retry chains to QA (privacy check).

Short action list (next steps):
- Marcus: prototype canonicalization hash script for 30k examples (1 week)
- Diego: add UI fields to triage form draft (CURATE-742) and send to Priya for review (3 days)
- Priya: seed weekly pool rules in spreadsheet and run first sample pass next Wed (50 examples)
- All: sync next Tue 9am to review first-pass results and adjust thresholds

Loose notes / thoughts:
- Keep heuristics conservative early: false positives (flagging low ROI) cost human time. But false negatives (missing blockers) cost customers. Bias towards recall for impact >=3.
- Document a couple canonicalization failures we saw in earlier run: date formats with timezone suffixes, escaped HTML in free text.

End of scratch.

(If I forget: this is a working doc; will refine after first pool run.)
